# Investment Memorandum

## 1. Executive Summary

- On 2022-03-18, Party City Holdings Inc. and Party City Corporation (the borrowers) entered into a sixth amendment to their ABL Credit Agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. as Administrative Agent and a syndicate of lenders.
- The borrowers are Delaware corporations operating in the party supplies and retail industry, with Party City Holdings Inc. serving as the Borrower Agent and Party City Corporation as the Subsidiary Borrower.
- This amendment modifies the definition of "Eligible In-Transit Inventory" in the original ABL Credit Agreement dated August 19, 2015 (as previously amended five times through February 2021).
- The purpose is to temporarily increase eligible in-transit inventory limits and extend shipping timeframes to provide additional borrowing capacity and operational flexibility. The amendment increases the aggregate limit for foreign-shipped eligible in-transit inventory from $50,000,000 to $75,000,000 temporarily (until January 2023 borrowing base certificate delivery), while extending the shipping timeframe from 60 to 75 days during this period.
- Party City is a leading party supplies retailer operating through multiple subsidiaries including Amscan Inc., Party Horizon Inc., and various specialty entities focused on party supplies, decorations, and related products.

## 2. Investment Highlights & Risks

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
• Strong lender syndicate including JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. (Administrative Agent), Bank of America N.A., Wells Fargo Bank, Credit Suisse AG, MUFG Union Bank N.A., TD Bank N.A., Bank of Montreal, and Goldman Sachs Bank USA, indicating broad institutional support
• Borrower representations confirm no defaults or events of default are occurring and continuing as of the amendment effective date
• All existing collateral documents and security interests remain in full force and effect, maintaining lender protection
• Amendment includes consent fees of $7,500 per participating lender, demonstrating borrower's willingness to compensate lenders for modifications

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
• The amendment relaxes inventory eligibility criteria by increasing limits and extending timeframes, which could indicate potential liquidity or operational challenges requiring additional borrowing capacity
• Asset-based lending structure inherently carries inventory valuation and liquidation risks
• Limited visibility into overall financial performance, liquidity metrics, or other covenant compliance from this amendment document alone
